result.title: To Learn is to Wander: Learning Across Graphs and Tasks with Random Walks
result.summary: Graph foundation models aim to transfer across graphs, feature spaces, relational schemas, and prediction tasks, yet existing approaches typically generalize only within particular graph modalities or tasks. We propose Wander, a graph foundation model designed to operate across these settings within a single pretrained checkpoint. Following the prior-predictive perspective, we formulate graph learning as completion of a partially observed graph. We realize this task-general view through a common interface based on random walks, allowing the same model to operate across homogeneous and multi-relational graphs with varying features, labels, and relational schemas. Wander can increase its structural context at inference time without changing its learned parameters and, under suitable assumptions, universally approximates the corresponding Bayes-optimal predictor on bounded connected graphs. Empirically, a single pretrained checkpoint achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive results across node classification, homogeneous link prediction, and knowledge-graph link prediction. Moreover, joint pretraining across graph modalities and tasks preserves performance in specialized settings while enabling positive transfer and the composition of separately learned capabilities at inference time.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Wander 图基础模型，把图学习统一表述为随机游走接口下的部分观测图补全，用单一预训练权重跨图模态与任务迁移，并支持推理时扩展结构上下文。
AI.relevance_reason: 随机游走作为统一接口、推理期扩展上下文而不改参数、以及“能力可组合”的设定，可能与 LVR 中证据获取与动态计算、latent 状态的证据筛选有概念呼应，但论文为图基础模型，与视觉多模态推理无直接关联，需人工核查是否具备方法迁移价值。
